transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 min
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam Ortega (Redwood); Sara Patel, Tomás Ruiz, Evelyn Moore (Helion Core)
Recording link: https://redwood.example/recordings/ff-20260403-helioncore

Summary (auto): quick readout of week 2 bench. Discussed 95th/99th latencies, throughput scaling behavior, and security/VPC constraints. Agreed on extra tail tests and traffic handoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:07] Sara Patel: Sara here, hi.
[00:09] Tomás Ruiz: Tomas Ruiz, platform.
[00:11] Evelyn Moore: Evelyn for CTO.
[00:13] Liam Ortega: Liam with Redwood SE, hi all.
[00:18] Maya Chen: cool, agenda — we'll walk through the numbers we published, highlight deltas vs your incumbent and then talk tuning and next steps.
[00:27] Sara Patel: sounds good, we got the sheet, thanks. small note the headers in the CSV got a little munged, so we trust your annotated view.
[00:36] Liam Ortega: right, so quick context — we ran the same prompt set you provided last week across two configs: hosted small-batch (our default) and dedicated 4-slot with batching thresholds you requested. Baseline is the incumbent vendor you shared.
[00:52] Tomás Ruiz: yes, baseline is CloudAI managed endpoints, roughly the same model family.
[00:58] Liam Ortega: ok, slide 1: average token latency — hosted default about 36ms/token, dedicated about 22ms/token, baseline reported ~45ms/token under your traffic. That maps to a 51% cost reduction estimate in our ballpark calc but we'll send the detailed unit-cost sheet.
[01:20] Sara Patel: hmm 36ms avg is good, but our users notice spikes. What about the 95th and 99th?
[01:27] Liam Ortega: good call — 95th is around 120ms on hosted, 78ms on dedicated; 99th sits at 310ms hosted vs 180ms dedicated. We did see occasional KV-cache warming on long contexts which increases tail.
[01:44] Maya Chen: note — transcription: K-V cash warming — that's KV cache, sometimes the exporter turned it into 'cash' lol.
[01:51] Evelyn Moore: that 99th still worries me, our SLA target is 200ms for critical flows.
[01:58] Liam Ortega: totally, and that's why we recommended two mitigations: prefix caching for common startup tokens and using our routing fallback to the lower-latency variant for latency-sensitive routes.
[02:10] Sara Patel: can you explain routing fallback again? the doc had a couple of options.
[02:15] Liam Ortega: yes so policy-wise you can route by latency SLO — if hosted variant spikes above threshold we failover to dedicated or a quantized lower-latency variant. There's also region-based fallback. It's configurable per route.
[02:28] Tomás Ruiz: we need that behavior inside our VPC; we can't have user tokens leaving the VPC for compliance.
[02:34] Maya Chen: understood — for VPC we do Private deployment or VPC peering for dedicated. For the POC we can provision a Private eval node behind your VPC, that keeps traffic in. We'll bring infra docs.
[02:46] Evelyn Moore: what's the overhead of private? is that going to push up latency compared to Redwood's hosted env?
[02:51] Liam Ortega: negligible if colocated in same cloud region; the added hop is mainly control plane. Runtime latency is roughly the same, sometimes slightly better because you avoid public egress.
[03:03] Sara Patel: ok. Another question on throughput — our goal is 80 qps sustained at 2 second p95 for the longest prompts. How did Redwood's dedicated config handle load?
[03:14] Liam Ortega: on the dedicated 4-slot we hit ~95 qps sustain with 1.8s p95 for the long prompts in our synthetic trace. Under your real trace (more bursty) throughput dipped to ~72 qps with occasional queueing; that's where autoscaling burst slots help.
[03:29] Tomás Ruiz: autoscaling — how fast? we can't have long cold starts.
[03:33] Liam Ortega: burst slots can spin up within 30–45s depending on GPU availability in the region; we can pre-warm slots based on traffic patterns. For strict SLOs we recommend a small warm buffer.
[03:44] Evelyn Moore: 30–45 seconds is a lot. we need to see how often that happens in our trace.
[03:48] Maya Chen: action: Tomás will share representative traffic trace; we can simulate and show frequency of cold-start events.
[03:54] Sara Patel: agreed. Also your cost calc assumed 16k context lengths, but many of our calls are shorter. can you re-run with 4k context to show delta?
[04:03] Liam Ortega: yes we can re-run with 4k; that usually improves throughput and reduces KV pressure. We'll add that to the artifacts.
[04:10] Sara Patel: perfect.
[04:12] [04:12] Liam Ortega: quick pause to call out an anomaly — during one of the hosted runs we saw a persistent 2x CPU process on the host which inflated tail for a 7‑minute window. we've marked that run as outlier.
[04:23] Maya Chen: yep, outliers excluded in the annotated sheet.
[04:26] Sara Patel: do you have a playbook for fallback thresholds? our SREs want explicit numbers.
[04:30] Liam Ortega: we recommend threshold flow: p95 > 250ms or error-rate > 0.5% triggers canary fallback to dedicated until metrics normalize. But those numbers are customizable per route.
[04:44] Tomás Ruiz: and logging — will we get token-level cost and trace?
[04:48] Maya Chen: yes, the Console provides token-level cost, per-route tracing, and error traces. For private deployments we can ship agent logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3.
[04:59] Evelyn Moore: SOC2 docs? our procurement will ask.
[05:02] Maya Chen: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts; I'll share the security pack.
[05:06] Sara Patel: great.
[05:08] Liam Ortega: ok back to tuning — small changes gave big tail improvements: lower batching window to 8ms for latency routes, bump KV prewarm to 3x instances. That trimmed 99th by ~30% in the dedicated tests.
[05:22] Sara Patel: would lowering batching increase cost?
[05:25] Liam Ortega: small increase in per-token cost, but tradeoff is improved SLA compliance. We'll quantify margin in the cost sheet.
[05:33] Tomás Ruiz: curious about quantization — did you test 4-bit variants?
[05:36] Liam Ortega: yes we tested q4f32 for a lower-latency variant; it shaved 10–15% latency but had mild regression on certain prompt completions — quality delta is in the eval sheet.
[05:50] Evelyn Moore: quality regressions are a no-go on critical flows. We can consider quantized variants only for non-critical routes.
[05:57] Maya Chen: good note.
[06:00] Sara Patel: any pricing delta for dedicated reserved slots vs on-demand?
[06:04] Maya Chen: reserved is 30–40% cheaper depending on commit term; we'll include a modeled TCO for your projected qps.
[06:13] Tomás Ruiz: about the baseline comparators — we've seen CloudAI's p95 spike during their maintenance windows. Do you have a playbook for cross‑vendor comparison during maintenance?
[06:24] Liam Ortega: we recommend synchronizing bench windows; otherwise compare stable windows only. We also expose trace tags to mark maintenance windows.
[06:32] Sara Patel: okay.
[06:34] Liam Ortega: small tangent — we noticed a few transcription artifacts in the sheet where 'route' became 'root' and so on.
[06:40] Sara Patel: lol noted.
[06:42] [06:42] Maya Chen: quick show of artifacts — link to annotated latency sheet, raw run logs, and unit cost model: https://redwood.example/artifacts/helioncore-week2.
[06:53] Tomás Ruiz: can you share the raw logs? our infra team wants them to validate tracing.
[06:57] Liam Ortega: yes raw logs included but compressed due to size; we'll hand off an S3 link with presigned access.
[07:04] Evelyn Moore: timeline — if we find dedicated meets SLOs, how long to spin a pilot reserved pool?
[07:10] Maya Chen: reserved pool provisioning typically 7–10 business days for capacity normalization and security onboarding. Private deployment adds 2–3 extra days depending on networking.
[07:22] Sara Patel: that's ok. procurement will want exact dates.
[07:25] Maya Chen: we'll put concrete dates in the follow-up.
[07:28] Tomás Ruiz: any more checks you recommend before handover to SREs?
[07:32] Liam Ortega: run the 99th tail test on dedicated with your real trace, validate prewarm behavior, and exercise failover scenarios. Also entropy tests for KV eviction patterns.
[07:45] Sara Patel: can you replicate one of our weekend heavy tails? it happens every Sunday at 03:00.
[07:50] Liam Ortega: yes we can schedule a run to mirror that pattern.
[07:53] Maya Chen: okay action recap in the next section.
[07:56] --- Recap / Action items ---
[07:58] Maya Chen: Tomás to upload trace by 04/05.
[08:02] Liam Ortega: I'll run 99th-pct tail tests and attach logs by 04/07.
[08:05] Maya Chen: I'll share the annotated latency spreadsheet and SOC2 pack by 04/06.
[08:09] Sara Patel: we'll review and aim for a decision on reserved slots by April 20.
[08:14] Evelyn Moore: procurement wants a rough NDA + pricing window; please include reserved pricing options.
[08:20] Maya Chen: will do.
[08:22] Sara Patel: thanks all, helpful session.
[08:24] Liam Ortega: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[08:27] Maya Chen: meeting adjourned.
